- Stock entities: `res/content/base/entities/` and `res/content/base/skeletons/`
  — authoritative, always up-to-date format examples.
- Real usage: `wooden_meat_game` `content/my_pack/` — `entities/`,
  `skeletons/`, `scripts/components/`, spawn items. (Contains the `"rigidbody"`
  bug documented above — do not treat as style guide.)

VCM/OBJ model formats are covered in 14-models.md; bone animation is
covered in 11-animation.md.


<!-- ===== docs/11-animation.md ===== -->

# 11. Animations (VCA Format, Preload, Playback, core:animator)

> **MANDATORY PREREQUISITES — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md) AND
> [08-pitfalls.md](08-pitfalls.md). 01 defines the ID rules, reserved names
> and trust labels this file relies on; 08 lists the real failure modes
> behind every DO/AVOID note. Skipping either is the most common reason
> models generate broken packs from this guide. If you received only this
> file, fetch and read both before writing any code.

This document covers the animation system of VoxelCore: the text-based VCA
format (`.vca` files), how tracks are loaded through `preload.json`, how to
play them from Lua (`animation.play`), and the built-in state-machine
component `core:animator`. It continues from 10-entities.md: entity
skeletons (bones) are described there, and every bone referenced by an
animation must exist in the entity's skeleton file.

What is OUT OF SCOPE here: creating/exporting animations in external tools,
the VCM 3D-model format itself (see 14-models.md), and camera
internals beyond playing a track on a camera.

## Mental model

- An **animation track** is a `.vca` text file in the pack folder `animation/`
  (singular spelling — an engine constant, do NOT "fix" it to `animations`).
  `[VERIFIED: engine source, ANIMATION_FOLDER]`
- A track is a set of **directives** (`@move`, `@rotate`, `@scale`, `@zoom`,
  `@texture`) that define scalar curves over time. Directive ORDER in the
  file does not matter — the engine applies transforms by channel and axis,
  not by file order. `[DOC]`
- Tracks are applied to a **target**: an entity skeleton (`entity.skeleton`)
  or a camera. Bone-targeted directives name the bone via the `bone`
  attribute. `[DOC]`
- Playback is a CLIENT-SIDE visual effect on the render skeleton. Playing a
  track mutates bone matrices of the local renderer; it does not change
  entity physics or position. `[VERIFIED: engine source, pose matrices]`
- The `.vca` parser is implemented in Lua inside the engine
  (`res/modules/internal/formats/vca.lua`) and compiles each track into a
  generated Lua function. Parse errors are LOUD (they throw); runtime lookups
  can be silent (see pitfalls). `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

## Loading tracks — preload.json and the FLAT namespace

Animations are NOT loaded automatically. A pack must list them in its
`preload.json` under the `"animation"` key. `[DOC: assets-preload]`

```json
{
    "animation": ["hit", "rip"]
}
```

How the engine resolves an entry — read this carefully, it defines the
naming rules: `[VERIFIED: engine source, AssetsLoader.cpp / assetload_funcs.cpp]`

1. The preload entry (e.g. `"hit"`) is used VERBATIM as the track name and as
   a path under the pack folder: the engine searches all content sources for
   `animation/hit.vca`.
2. The name is NOT prefixed with the pack id. Unlike blocks and items
   (`my_pack:my_block`), animation names live in ONE GLOBAL FLAT namespace:
   `animation.play("hit", ...)` — bare name, no colon.
3. If the file does not exist, preload SILENTLY SKIPS it (no error at load
   time). The failure surfaces later: `animation.play` on a missing track
   logs an engine error `animation track not found` and the playback entry is
   dropped.

DO namespace your track names: use subfolders in the preload entry and the
folder tree — `"animation": ["guns/recoil", "mobs/imp_idle"]` loads
`animation/guns/recoil.vca` under the name `guns/recoil`. Longer unique names
are the ONLY protection against cross-pack collisions.

- AVOID short generic track names like `"hit"`, `"idle"`, `"walk"`. Another
  pack preloading the same name overwrites yours (the engine stores tracks
  by bare name, last load wins), and your `animation.play("hit")` may even
  resolve to the OTHER pack's file — name resolution searches all content
  sources, not just your pack. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
- Real-world example: wooden_meat_game preloads `"hit"`, `"rip"` — short and
  collision-prone; it simply got lucky. Do not copy that naming.

Runtime loading from a string is also available (advanced):
`assets.parse_animation("vca", content_string, "my_name")` — parses a VCA
text and registers it under the given name. `[DOC: libassets]`

## VCA syntax primer

VCA uses the VCM text syntax (the engine's model-format syntax): directives
look like XML tags, written `@tag attr value attr2 "quoted value"` with an
optional `{ ... }` block of child directives. `[DOC: vcm.md]`

- Attributes take bare words (`curve linear`), quoted strings
  (`bone "body"` — quotes optional for single words), parenthesized vectors
  (`origin (0.5,0.5,0.5)` — not used by VCA), or `{ ... }` blocks (children).
- Indentation and line breaks are insignificant; one directive per line is
  the convention. The example repo uses TAB indentation — this guide shows
  4 spaces; both parse identically.
- A `.vca` file has no explicit root element; the whole file is one implicit
  `track`. `[VERIFIED: engine source, xml.parse_vcd(source, "track")]`

## Directive reference

| Directive | Applies to | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@move` | skeleton bone, camera, object | Translate by offset, per axis |
| `@rotate` | skeleton bone, camera, object | Rotate by angle, per axis — DEGREES |
| `@scale` | skeleton bone, object | Scale multiplier, per axis |
| `@zoom` | camera only | Camera zoom multiplier |
| `@texture` | skeleton only | Swap a dynamic texture slot over time |

`[DOC: vca.md]`

Common attributes: `[DOC + VERIFIED: parser]`

- `bone "name"` — target a bone of the skeleton by name. Directives WITHOUT
  `bone` target the whole object (camera/object transforms); `@texture`
  instead uses `name "$slot"` to pick the texture slot.
- `by x` / `by y` / `by z` — which scalar the curve drives. MUST be exactly
  one letter `x`, `y` or `z` (anything else is silently computed and never
  applied). `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
- `curve const|linear|bezier` or `curve .my_custom` — keyframe curve type
  (see below).
- `func (expression)` — expression curve instead of keyframes (see below).
- `period N` — loop THIS line every N frames (see below).

One line = one directive = one scalar curve. A bone can have up to three
`@move` lines (`by x/y/z`), three `@rotate` lines, three `@scale` lines.

- AVOID two lines of the same channel+axis on the same bone (e.g. two
  `@move bone "body" by y`). The engine keeps only the LAST one — the
  earlier line is silently discarded. `[VERIFIED: engine source, codegen]`

## Time model — configure, frames, duration (read twice)

Meta-information is set with a `@configure` directive; it applies GLOBALLY
no matter where it sits in the file, but DO put it at the top:

```vca
@configure fps 30 frames 15 rotation-order XYZ
```

`[DOC: vca.md]`

- `fps` — frame rate DIVISOR for duration computation. Default: `60`.
- `frames` — frame count (DIVIDEND). Track duration = `frames / fps`
  seconds. A keyframe `frame N` therefore means "at N ticks of 1/fps
  seconds": with default fps 60, frame 12 = 0.2 s; with fps 30, frame 12 =
  0.4 s. `[DOC + VERIFIED: engine source, DEFAULT_FPS = 60]`
- `duration` — explicit duration in seconds; overrides `frames`. The
  upstream docs note that keyframe curves REQUIRE `fps` (or `frames`) via
  configure or explicit `duration`.
- `rotation-order` — Euler application order (`XYZ`, `ZYX`, ...) for
  `@rotate` lines, because file order is NOT honored. Default `XYZ`.

**The dangerous default: a track with NO `configure` never ends.**
`[VERIFIED: engine source]` The parser initializes duration to `math.huge`
and only a `configure` directive (or explicit `duration`) shrinks it. The
playback loop stops a track only when its timer exceeds duration — so a
track without configure runs FOREVER, holding the pose of its last keyframe
values (keyframe curves clamp to the last value; expression curves keep
evaluating forever).

This is not always a bug — it is a pattern: wooden_meat_game's `rip.vca`
(death animation) intentionally has no configure, so the entity stays in its
fallen pose permanently. For action clips (recoil, hits) the same default
just means the clip freezes at its final values — which is harmless ONLY if
the final values are the rest pose (0).

DO end action keyframes at the rest pose (value 0) unless you intentionally
freeze a pose.
DO give looping idle/walk tracks either no configure plus `period` on each
line, or a `configure` and a driver that loops (see core:animator).

## Keyframe curves (curve const / linear / bezier)

A keyframe curve drives `f(t)` by interpolating between `@key` directives in
the directive's `{ ... }` block:

```vca
@rotate bone "body" by z curve linear {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 6 value 45
    @key frame 12 value 0
}
```

Curve types: `[DOC: vca.md]`

- `const` — no interpolation: the value jumps at each keyframe.
- `linear` — piecewise-linear interpolation (the everyday choice).
- `bezier` — cubic Bezier between keys with explicit tangents; a bezier key
  carries `lx ly rx ry` — tangent handle OFFSETS relative to the key's own
  frame (`lx`, `rx`) and value (`ly`, `ry`). `[VERIFIED: engine source,
  codegen adds them to the key's frame/value]` Hand-writing bezier keys is
  rare — exporters produce them.

Each key needs `frame N` (in fps ticks) and `value V` (a number — EXCEPT the
`@texture` directive, whose values are texture name strings, stepped
const-style). `[DOC + VERIFIED]`

Texture example from the upstream docs (slot `$0`, stepping between two
faces of a tireman entity):

```vca
@texture name $0 {
    @key frame 0 value entities/tireman:face_0
    @key frame 24 value entities/tireman:face_1
}
```

Looping one line: add `period N` (in frames) to wrap that line's time
modulo N — useful for endless idle motions in a track without `configure`:

```vca
@move by y curve linear period 24 {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 12 value 1
    @key frame 24 value 0
}
```

`[DOC: vca.md]`

- Keyframes do NOT need to start at frame 0; before the first key the curve
  clamps to the first value.
- DO keep keyframe `frame` numbers ordered and within `frames` from
  `configure` if you set one.

## Expression curves (func)

Instead of keyframes, a line can define `f(t) = value` directly, where `t`
is time in SECONDS:

```vca
@move bone "antenna" by y func (sin(t * 2.5) * 0.1)
```

`[DOC: vca.md]`

Expressions are transpiled into a Lua function body. Documented operators:
`+ * / % ^`; constants `pi`, `e`. `[DOC]`

The ACTUAL function set available inside VCA expressions (verified against
the engine's codegen environment — this differs from the upstream doc!):
`[VERIFIED: engine source, animation_codegen.lua]`

| Available | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `sqrt min max floor ceil abs sign round exp` | standard math |
| `sin cos tan` | trigonometry (radians) |
| `deg rad log log10` | unit conversion, logarithms |
| `noise(x, octaves)` | 1D smooth pseudo-noise, range about -1..1 |
| `pi e` | constants |
| `t` | time in seconds (only in `func` lines) |
| `kl kr` | left/right keyframe objects (`.value`, `.frame`) — only in custom curves |

Documented but NOT actually available — using them raises a runtime nil-call
error when the track plays: `[VERIFIED: engine source — not in the codegen
environment]`

- `rand(low, high)` — listed in `doc/*/vca.md`, absent from the codegen env.
- `noise2d(x, y, octaves)` — the math library exports `noise2d`, but the
  codegen binds a name that does not exist, so neither `noise2d` nor
  `noise2` works in VCA expressions.

DO verify any function beyond the table above with a quick in-engine test
before relying on it — the upstream doc and the code disagree here.

## Custom curves (@curve)

Declare a reusable interpolation curve, then reference it with a leading
dot: `[DOC: vca.md]`

```vca
@curve ease-in-out func (kl.value + (kr.value - kl.value) * (t * t * (3 - 2 * t)))

@move bone "body" by y curve .ease-in-out {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 12 value 1
}
```

Inside `@curve func`, `t` is the 0..1 position BETWEEN the two neighboring
keys, `kl`/`kr` are the left/right keyframes (`kl.value`, `kr.value`).
`[DOC + VERIFIED]`

## Units and transform semantics

- `@rotate` values are **DEGREES**. The engine's `mat4.rotate` converts to
  radians internally: `value 90` is a quarter turn. `[VERIFIED: engine
  source, libmat4.cpp applies glm::radians]` (The upstream docs never state
  the unit.)
- `@move` values are in world blocks — the same units as skeleton node
  offsets (see 10-entities.md). Values like `0.25` are typical for a recoil
  kick; `hit.vca` below uses exactly that.
- `@scale` and `@zoom` are multipliers (`1` = unchanged).
- Multiple `@rotate` lines on one bone are applied in `rotation-order`
  (default `XYZ`), NOT in file order. `[DOC + VERIFIED]`
- Move/rotate/scale compose as a matrix applied to the bone's bind-pose
  matrix each frame.

## Playing tracks — animation.play

The `animation` library (global) is small: `[DOC: libanimation.md,
RU-only upstream]`

```lua
animation.play(name, target)  -- returns a playing-track handle
animation.action(func)        -- run a coroutine outside pause, dies on world exit
```

`animation.play` in detail: `[VERIFIED: engine source, animation.lua]`

```lua
local handle = animation.play("guns/recoil", entity.skeleton)
```

- The target's pose is RESET (to bind pose) at play time, then re-reset and
  re-applied EVERY frame while the track runs.
- Returns a handle object with UNDOCUMENTED control methods:
  `handle:stop()` (stop and reset timer), `handle:pause()`,
  `handle:resume()`. `[OBSERVED: engine source]`
- Playing a second track on the same target does not stop the first, but the
  newer track applies LATER each frame and its pose reset wipes the older
  track's output — in practice the last-played track wins visually.
  `[VERIFIED: engine source, playback loop order]`
- Playing an unknown name logs `animation track not found` and does nothing.

Targets: `[DOC: animation.md, RU-only upstream]`

```lua
-- 1. An entity skeleton (the normal case):
animation.play("mobs/imp_walk", entity.skeleton)

-- 2. A camera:
local camera = cameras.get(cameras.index("my_pack:cutscene_cam"))
animation.play("cutscenes/flyover", camera)
```

Camera targets use directives WITHOUT `bone`: `@move`/`@rotate` drive the
camera transform, `@zoom` drives zoom. `[DOC + VERIFIED: codegen camera path]`

The first-person hand skeleton is also addressable via
`gfx.skeletons.get("hand")` — same API surface as entity skeletons (see
`doc/*/scripting/builtins/libgfx-skeletons.md`). `[DOC]`

Where to call `play` from: any client-side Lua — component scripts
(`health.lua` in wooden_meat_game plays `hit` when damaged), HUD scripts, or
layout companion scripts (see 09-hud-and-ui.md). `[OBSERVED]`

## Runtime behavior every author must know

`[VERIFIED: engine source, animation.lua]` unless noted:

- Tracks advance per RENDERED frame (`time.delta()` per frame), so playback
  is a client-side visual only; pausing and world changes are handled by the
  engine (tracks are unloaded with the world).
- While a track runs, the target pose is reset to bind pose EVERY FRAME and
  only the animated channels are applied on top. Manual bone edits (e.g.
  `skeleton:set_matrix`) made elsewhere get overwritten while a track plays.
- When a track ENDS (timer exceeds duration), the pose stays at the last
  applied state — there is NO automatic return to rest. Either end your
  keyframes at rest values, or call `entity.skeleton:reset_pose()` yourself.
- There is no built-in "queue" or "on finish" callback. For state-driven
  characters use `core:animator` (below) or drive tracks from your own
  component.

## core:animator — the built-in state machine

For skeletons that switch between looping states (idle/walk/attack), the
engine ships a component: `core:animator`. The upstream doc marks it as
"under development" — treat its interface as provisional. `[DOC + OBSERVED:
engine source, res/scripts/components/animator.lua]`

What it does (from the engine's own script): `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

- Maintains named STATES, each bound to a track name.
- On `set_state(name, fade_time)` it cross-fades: the new state fades in and
  the old one fades out over `fade_time` seconds using the track function's
  `intensity` parameter (multiplier channels fade correctly, additive
  channels scale toward 0).
- On every render frame it resets the skeleton pose and evaluates ALL active
  states, looping each track's time modulo its duration — so state tracks
  loop automatically regardless of `configure`.

DO use `core:animator` for mob-style looping states instead of hand-rolling
play/stop bookkeeping; keep one-shot action clips (hit, death) on plain
`animation.play` from your gameplay scripts, as wooden_meat_game does.

Manual rig manipulation (no VCA at all) is also legitimate — the base
pack's `player_animator` component positions the held item every frame with
`rig:index("item")`, `rig:set_model(index, ...)`, `rig:set_matrix(index,
mat4.rotate({0, 1, 0}, -80))`. Mix deliberately, not accidentally: while a
VCA track plays, its per-frame pose reset erases manual `set_matrix` edits.

## Real annotated examples (verbatim, wooden_meat_game)

Registered in `content/my_pack/preload.json`:

```json
{
    "animation": ["hit", "rip"]
}
```

`hit.vca` — one-shot recoil on the `body` bone; NOTE: no `configure`, so the
track technically runs forever while clamping to the last (rest) values:

```vca
@rotate bone "body" by y curve linear {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 2 value 7
    @key frame 6 value -7
    @key frame 10 value 7
    @key frame 12 value 0
}

@move bone "body" by y curve linear {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 6 value 0.25
    @key frame 12 value 0
}
```

Line by line: `[OBSERVED]`

- `@rotate ... by y` — yaw shake: +7 degrees at frame 2 (= 2/60 s at default
  fps 60), over-corrects to -7, settles at 0 by frame 12 (= 0.2 s).
- `@move ... by y` — a 0.25-block lift peaking mid-clip, back to 0.
- Both lines end at value 0 — the rest pose — so the infinite-duration
  default is harmless here.

`rip.vca` — death clip that FREEZES the fallen pose on purpose:

```vca
@rotate bone "body" by x curve linear {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 18 value 90
}

@move bone "body" by y curve linear {
    @key frame 0 value 0
    @key frame 18 value 0
    @key frame 19 value -100
}
```

- Rotates the body 90 degrees around X (falls over — degrees, as verified
  above), then yanks it 100 blocks down at the last frame (sinks it out of
  sight). No configure: the pose persists forever. That is the intended
  "rest in peace" behavior.

Playback, from the pack's health component:

```lua
animation.play("hit", entity.skeleton)
```

- Bare track name (flat namespace), entity skeleton as target. The full
  component context is in 10-entities.md.

## Pitfalls

1. **Plural spellings.** Folder `animations/` or preload key `"animations"`
   load nothing. The engine constant is `animation` (singular).
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]` (Also listed in 08-pitfalls.md.)
2. **Expecting pack prefixes.** `animation.play("my_pack:hit", ...)` finds
   nothing — track names are bare preload entries in a flat global
   namespace. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
3. **Inventing fields.** A typo in a directive or attribute name is a LOUD
   parse error (`unknown directive ...`) the moment the pack loads — the
   opposite of entity JSON, where unknown fields are silently ignored. But
   attribute VALUE typos can stay silent: a wrong `by` letter computes and
   applies nothing. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
4. **Bone name typos.** `skeleton:index(name)` returns nil for an unknown
   bone; in the Lua fallback path nil becomes bone index 0 and the animation
   silently animates the FIRST bone. No error is thrown. Check bone names
   against your `skeletons/<name>.json`. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
5. **Trust the duration default.** Without `configure` the track never ends
   (duration = infinity). For one-shot clips always end keyframes at rest
   values — or the pose freezes mid-motion forever.
6. **Playing a track that was never preloaded.** Preload silently skips
   missing files; `play` then errors `animation track not found` at runtime.
   Register the track in `preload.json` and check the spelling.
7. **Assuming auto-return or auto-loop.** Neither exists in `animation.play`:
   finished tracks keep their last pose, and looping only happens via
   `period`, an infinite default, or core:animator's modulo.
8. **Calling `rand`/`noise2d` in expressions.** They are documented upstream
   but absent from the codegen environment — the track fails at play time.
   Use the verified function table above. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
9. **Two same-channel lines on one bone.** The last one silently wins; split
   complex motion across bones or merge keys into one line.

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO list every `.vca` in `preload.json` under `"animation"` (singular).
- DO namespace track names (`"guns/recoil"`, `"mobs/imp_walk"`) — the
  namespace is global and collision-prone.
- DO put a `@configure` at the top when the track must END; end action clips
  at rest values otherwise.
- DO end keyframes at value 0 for one-shot clips unless freezing is intended.
- DO use `core:animator` for looping character states; keep one-shots on
  `animation.play`.
- DO recheck bone names against the skeleton file — typos animate bone #0
  silently.
- AVOID `animations` (plural) anywhere: not the folder, not the key.
- AVOID pack prefixes in `animation.play` names.
- AVOID relying on `rand`, `noise2d` or any function outside the verified
  expression table.
- AVOID two lines of the same channel+axis on the same bone — the last one
  silently replaces the first.

## Upstream pointers (read before writing real animations)

The paths below are files of the ENGINE's own repository
(github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore, folder `doc/`) — NOT files of this guide.
The Russian documentation is usually MORE complete and more current; when the
two diverge, prefer `doc/ru/`:

| Topic | English (`doc/en/`) | Russian (`doc/ru/`) — prefer this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Animation system overview | — (no EN file) | `doc/ru/animation.md` |
| VCA format reference | `doc/en/vca.md` | `doc/ru/vca.md` |
| VCM syntax (shared grammar) | `doc/en/vcm.md` | `doc/ru/vcm.md` |
| Skeletons, rigging, bone format | `doc/en/rigging.md` | `doc/ru/rigging.md` |
| `animation.*` Lua API | — (no EN file) | `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libanimation.md` |
| Skeleton object API (`set_texture`, ...) | `doc/en/scripting/builtins/libgfx-skeletons.md` | `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libgfx-skeletons.md` |
| Camera targets (`cameras.*`) | `doc/en/scripting/builtins/libcameras.md` | `doc/ru/scripting/builtins/libcameras.md` |
| Preload categories | `doc/en/assets-preload.md` | `doc/ru/assets-preload.md` |

Where this guide's claims go beyond the upstream text (degrees in `@rotate`,
the infinite-duration default, the flat namespace, the exact expression
function table, the returned handle methods), they were verified against the
engine's source code and Lua internals at the time of writing — re-verify
against your engine version if behavior seems to differ.

Real usage to learn from: `wooden_meat_game` `content/my_pack/` —
`animation/hit.vca`, `animation/rip.vca`, `preload.json`, and
`scripts/components/health.lua` (one `animation.play` call). The engine's
own `res/scripts/components/animator.lua` is the reference implementation of
the state-machine pattern.


<!-- ===== docs/12-sounds.md ===== -->

# 12. Sounds and Audio (Preload, Playback, Streams)

> **MANDATORY PREREQUISITES — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md) AND
> [08-pitfalls.md](08-pitfalls.md). 01 defines the ID rules, reserved names
> and trust labels this file relies on; 08 lists the real failure modes
> behind every DO/AVOID note. Skipping either is the most common reason
> models generate broken packs from this guide. If you received only this
> file, fetch and read both before writing any code.

This document covers the audio subsystem as seen from a content pack: which
sound files a pack ships and how they are declared in `preload.json`, how
short preloaded sounds differ from streamed audio, how playback is controlled
through speaker ids and channels, and how block materials wire
step/place/break/hit sounds. Read the pitfalls section even if you skim the
API parts: the audio API fails SILENTLY (returns `0`, plays nothing, logs
nothing) in more situations than any other subsystem in this guide, so a
typo usually looks like "the code ran fine but there is no sound".

Out of scope here: runtime audio generation (`audio.PCMStream`, mic input) —
moved to 13-sound-creation.md. Authoring audio files in external tools and
OpenAL backend internals are out of scope entirely.

## Mental model: Sound vs Stream

Two different playable objects exist, and picking the wrong one is the
first pitfall:

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Sound | Fully loaded into RAM at pack load; one asset can play from many speakers at once; requires a `preload.json` entry; addressed by a short NAME without extension |
| Stream | Read from disk while playing; NOT preloaded, not stored in RAM; only one speaker per stream at a time; addressed by a FILE PATH with extension (or a shared alias) |
| Speaker | One-shot playback controller with a unique integer id; destroyed when the audio finishes or `audio.stop()` is called; survives pause |
| Channel | Volume/pause grouping: `master`, `ui`, `regular`, `ambient`, `music` |
| PCMStream | Lua-side source of raw PCM data; can be `share()`d as a stream alias or turned into a Sound via `create_sound` (13-sound-creation.md) |

`[DOC]` Decision rule:

- short, repeatable effects (steps, shots, clicks) that may overlap with
  themselves → preloaded Sound via `audio.play_sound` / `audio.play_sound_2d`
- long audio (music, ambience, radio) that must not sit in RAM → Stream via
  `audio.play_stream` / `audio.play_stream_2d`
- audio generated at runtime → build a `audio.PCMStream`, then either
  `share()` it as a stream or materialize a Sound with `create_sound`
  (13-sound-creation.md)

Formats: OGG (preferred) and WAV. WAV supports 8 and 16 bit only — 24 bit
is not supported by OpenAL. `[DOC]`

## Channels

| Channel | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| master | Controls the loudness of ALL other channels; NEVER pass it as a playback channel |
| ui | Interface sounds; not paused together with the game |
| regular | Default for world sounds; paused together with the game |
| ambient | Same pause behavior as regular; intended for background/weather loops |
| music | Music playback, typically streamed |

`[DOC]` Three hard facts the table hides:

- An UNKNOWN channel name behaves like `master`: the play call returns `0`
  and nothing plays, with no error. `[VERIFIED: engine source, libaudio.cpp]`
- `regular` (the default) pauses with the game; if you start an ambience
  loop on the default channel it will freeze during pause — use `ambient`
  or `music` for anything that should keep its state sensibly managed.
- Screen switches RESET `regular` and `ambient` to empty: every speaker and
  stream on them is stopped and destroyed (menu ↔ world transitions,
  including the moment a world finishes opening — see Streams). `ui` and
  `music` survive screen switches. `[VERIFIED: engine source,
  Engine::setScreen]`

## Shipping sounds: `preload.json` and the variants pattern

Sound files live under the pack's `sounds/` folder. Declare them in the
pack's `preload.json`: sounds are NOT loaded by default; a sound that is
not preloaded cannot be played with `audio.play_sound` at all. `[DOC]` Two entry forms:

```json
{
    "sounds": [
        "events/explosion",
        {
            "name": "events/explosion",
            "keep-pcm": true
        }
    ]
}
```

- string form: `"sounds/<name>.ogg"` (or `.wav`) is loaded under the name
  `<name>` — e.g. entry `"events/explosion"` loads
  `sounds/events/explosion.ogg` and is played as `"events/explosion"`.
- object form: adds `"keep-pcm": true`, which retains PCM data in memory
  after decoding. Only needed if you access raw samples; otherwise omit it
  (decoded PCM is the main RAM cost of a Sound). `[DOC]`

### Variant pattern (multiple files under one name)

Preload ONE logical name, ship several files; the engine collects them
automatically. `[VERIFIED: engine source, assetload::sound]`

| File present | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `name.ogg` | base sound (tried first) |
| `name_0.ogg` | base sound if `name.ogg` is absent — numbering MAY start at 0 |
| `name_1.ogg` .. `name_N.ogg` | variants, loaded until the FIRST missing number |
| `name_2.ogg` with no `name_1.ogg` | NEVER loaded — a numbering gap silently ends the list |

At play time the engine picks uniformly at random between the base sound
and all variants — the base is one of the choices, not a guaranteed
default. `[VERIFIED: engine source, audio.cpp]`

Hard rules:

1. Extensions are tried in order `.ogg`, then `.wav`; only ONE extension is
   used for the base AND all its variants (decided by which file exists for
   the base). `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
2. If neither `name.ext` nor `name_0.ext` exists, pack loading FAILS with
   `could not to find sound: sounds/<name>` — a typo in `preload.json`
   breaks the whole pack, it does not degrade gracefully. `[VERIFIED]`
3. Variant files must be MONO if the sound is played positionally (see the
   stereo warning below).

## Playing preloaded sounds: `audio.play_sound` / `_2d`

```lua
-- positional: audible from a point in the world, attenuates with distance
audio.play_sound(
    name,     -- preloaded sound NAME: no pack prefix, no "sounds/", no extension, no _N suffix
    x, y, z,  -- world position of the source
    volume,   -- 0.0 .. 1.0
    pitch,    -- playback speed multiplier, positive (1.0 = normal)
    -- optional:
    channel,  -- "regular" (default) / "ambient" / "music" / "ui"
    loop      -- false (default)
) -> speakerid

-- non-positional: same minus position; use for UI and menu sounds
audio.play_sound_2d(name, volume, pitch, --[[ optional: ]] channel, loop)
    -> speakerid
```

`[DOC: audio.md]` Name format is the #1 source of silent failures:

| You pass | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `"shotgun"` | plays `pack sounds/shotgun.ogg` (assuming this pack preloaded it) |
| `"steps/stone"` | plays preloaded `sounds/steps/stone.ogg` — subfolders are part of the name |
| `"sounds/shotgun"` | SILENT no-op — the name never includes the folder root |
| `"shotgun.ogg"` | SILENT no-op — no extension in the name |
| `"other_pack:shotgun"` | SILENT no-op — `play_sound` does NOT understand pack prefixes |

The returned speaker id is `0` in every failure case: unknown name, unknown
channel, or the NoAudio backend (no audio device / `[audio] enabled=false`).
`0` is a valid-looking integer — DO NOT treat it as an error by crashing;
DO check it once when debugging "why is there no sound".
`[VERIFIED: engine source, libaudio.cpp]`

Real examples from `wooden_meat_game` (`content/my_pack/`,
simplified to the audio calls): `[OBSERVED]`

```lua
-- scripts/shotgun.lua — local "2D" shot with two pitch layers
function on_use(pid)
    audio.play_sound_2d("shotgun", 0.5, 0.6)
    audio.play_sound_2d("shotgun", 0.5, 0.4)
end

-- scripts/components/turret_targeting.lua — positional shot at a world point
audio.play_sound("shotgun", start_pos[1], start_pos[2], start_pos[3], 0.6, 0.6)
audio.play_sound("shotgun", start_pos[1], start_pos[2], start_pos[3], 0.6, 0.4)
```

Playing the same sound twice with slightly different `pitch` is a cheap
layering trick that reads as one thicker shot. `[OBSERVED]`

## Streams: `audio.play_stream` / `_2d`

```lua
audio.play_stream(
    filename, -- stream address, SEE THE TABLE BELOW — NOT a preload name
    x, y, z,  -- world position
    volume,   -- 0.0 .. 1.0
    pitch,    -- positive multiplier
    -- optional:
    channel,  -- "regular" (default) / "ambient" / "music" / "ui"
    loop      -- false (default)
) -> speakerid

audio.play_stream_2d(filename, volume, pitch, --[[ optional: ]] channel, loop)
    -> speakerid
```

`[DOC: audio.md]` Streams need NO `preload.json` entry — that is their
point: the file is read from disk while playing, so a long OGG costs no
RAM. `[DOC]` The stream address is resolved in THREE different ways, in
this order: `[VERIFIED: engine source, libaudio.cpp — only the 2nd/3rd are
in the upstream doc]`

| Form | Example | Resolved as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared alias | `"test-stream"` | A name published by `stream:share(alias)` at runtime (see 13-sound-creation.md) |
| Entry-point path | `"my_pack:sounds/music.ogg"` | Literal file inside that pack — WITH extension |
| Bare path | `"sounds/music.ogg"` | `paths.find()` across ALL packs by content-source priority — WITH extension, collision-prone |

Hard rules for streams:

1. ONE stream can play through only ONE speaker at a time. To restart a
   music/ambience file, `audio.stop(old_id)` first — playing it again while
   the old speaker lives is a silent mistake. `[DOC]`
2. DO NOT preload long audio as Sounds: a 5-minute OGG as a Sound is fully
   decoded into RAM and stays there. Sounds are for short effects; streams
   are for anything measured in tens of seconds or minutes.
3. A stream speaker is destroyed when the file finishes (unless looping) or
   `audio.stop()` is called. Keep the returned id if you plan to touch
   volume/position later. `[DOC]`
4. On the NoAudio backend / headless mode the play calls return `0`; code
   that stores and then uses the id must tolerate that.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

Real pattern from `content/sfx/` in `wooden_meat_game` — an ambience pack
that ships NO `preload.json` at all: `[OBSERVED]`

```lua
-- content/sfx/modules/ambient.lua (simplified)
local BROWN = "sounds/pixabay.com_brown_noise___themediaguy-....ogg"

function ambient.on_hud_open()
    -- channel "ambient", loop=true, start almost muted
    field_stream = audio.play_stream_2d(BROWN, 0.05, 1.0, "ambient", true)
    wind_stream = audio.play_stream_2d(PINK, 0.0, 1.0, "ambient", true)
end

function ambient.on_world_tick()
    -- ...gust state machine computes wind_volume...
    audio.set_volume(wind_stream, wind_volume)
end
```

Note the file naming: long unique filenames (source-prefixed) instead of a
collision-free subfolder — same idea, protecting the BARE-path resolution
from other packs. `[OBSERVED]`

Also note that the example starts ambience from `scripts/hud.lua`
(`on_hud_open`) — that is the only correct place for ambient loops, not a
style choice. World-open sequence, from the engine source:

1. `on_world_open` fires (world.lua context) while the level screen is
   still being constructed.
2. The level screen then finishes opening — the gap is the initial chunk
   loading, observable as roughly half a second `[OBSERVED]` — and the
   engine resets the `regular` AND `ambient` channels
   (`Engine::setScreen`): every speaker and stream started in step 1 is
   destroyed here, silently.
3. `on_hud_open` fires AFTER the reset (hud.lua context), so loops started
   there survive into gameplay.

`[VERIFIED: engine source]` DO start all ambient/music world loops from
`on_hud_open` and nowhere else. The same reset also wipes
`regular`/`ambient` when the engine returns to the menu; `ui`/`music`
channels survive screen switches.

## Mono vs stereo — the positional audio trap

> Sounds played through OpenAL in STEREO ignore the source position
> entirely — they always render as if non-positional. Any sound you pass a
> world position to (`audio.play_sound`, `audio.play_stream`) must be MONO.
> `[DOC: audio.md WARNING]`

This bites silently: a stereo file plays "fine" in `_2d` calls, then sounds
mysterious when played positionally. DO export positional sounds in mono;
keep stereo only for music/UI. DO test positional sounds from a distance,
not standing on the source.

## Controlling a speaker

All functions take the integer speaker id returned by a play call. Calling
anything on a dead/finished/never-existed id is a silent no-op — nothing
throws. `[DOC]`

| Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `audio.stop(id)` | Stop and destroy the speaker |
| `audio.pause(id)` / `audio.resume(id)` | Pause / unpause (speaker survives pause) |
| `audio.set_loop(id, state)` / `audio.is_loop(id)` | Looping flag / read it back (`false` if id is dead) |
| `audio.set_volume(id, v)` / `audio.get_volume(id)` | 0.0..1.0 (`0.0` if id is dead) |
| `audio.set_pitch(id, p)` / `audio.get_pitch(id)` | positive multiplier (`1.0` if id is dead) |
| `audio.set_time(id, t)` / `audio.get_time(id)` | Position in SECONDS (`0.0` if id is dead) |
| `audio.set_position(id, x, y, z)` / `audio.get_position(id)` | World position (`nil` if id is dead) |
| `audio.set_velocity(id, x, y, z)` / `audio.get_velocity(id)` | Source velocity for the Doppler effect (`nil` if dead) |
| `audio.get_duration(id)` | Length in seconds; `0` also means "unknown" (e.g. radio-style streams) |
| `audio.count_speakers()` / `audio.count_streams()` | Diagnostics: live speakers / playing streams |

`[DOC]` Usage notes:

- Speaker ids start at 1, are never reused during the engine's lifetime,
  and `0` means "nothing was created". Store the id (an integer), not any
  reference. `[DOC]`
- Start ambience streams MUTED (`volume 0.0`) and ramp `set_volume` from a
  tick handler — this is exactly how the `sfx` pack animates wind gusts.
  `[OBSERVED]`
- For a moving source, update `set_position` periodically (e.g. from an
  entity tick), otherwise the sound stays where it started.
- `get_duration` returning `0` is NOT an error indicator — for generated
  and radio-style streams the length is legitimately unknown. `[DOC]`

## Sounds attached to blocks (materials)

Block materials carry four sound names plus an absorption factor — this is
how blocks get step/place/break/hit audio without any Lua
(see 05-textures-and-assets.md for the materials system itself):

```json
{
    "steps-sound": "steps/ground",
    "place-sound": "blocks/ground_place",
    "break-sound": "blocks/ground_break",
    "hit-sound": "blocks/ground_hit",
    "sound-absorption": 0.7
}
```

`[VERIFIED: engine source + res/content/base/block_materials/ground.json]`

Facts that save debugging time:

1. These sounds are loaded AUTOMATICALLY by the engine for every material —
   they do NOT need `preload.json` entries (the base pack's own preload
   lists none of them). `[VERIFIED: engine source, AssetsLoader::addDefaults]`
2. A material's sound name resolves inside the pack's `sounds/` folder:
   `"steps/ground"` → `sounds/steps/ground.ogg` of the pack defining the
   material — the `sounds/` root is added by the engine, you never write it
   in the material. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
3. If `hit-sound` is omitted it FALLS BACK to `steps-sound`.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source, ContentLoader::loadBlockMaterial]`
4. `sound-absorption` (0..1) scales how loud block sounds are for this
   material; stock values like `0.7` (ground) are a reference point.
   `[OBSERVED: stock pack values]`
5. The same `*-sound` keys are also accepted per-block in block JSON
   (`Block.cpp` parses them for every block), but the material is the
   primary mechanism the stock pack uses — prefer materials.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
6. Sound names used in materials share the SAME flat global namespace as
   `play_sound` names — two packs defining a material sound named
   `"steps/stone"` collide (see Pitfalls #2).

## Pitfalls (audio-specific)

1. **Silent no-op instead of an error.** Unknown sound name, unknown
   channel, dead speaker id, NoAudio backend — every one of these just
   returns `0` / does nothing. When "sound doesn't play", FIRST verify the
   returned speaker id and the exact name string before suspecting files.
   `[VERIFIED]`
2. **Flat global namespace.** Preload names are registered exactly as
   written, with NO pack prefix, and later registrations overwrite earlier
   ones; bare stream paths resolve across packs by priority. Two packs
   shipping `"explosion"` (or `"sounds/explosion.ogg"` as a bare stream
   path) will silently share/win by load order. DO namespace: put sounds in
   a subfolder (`"events/my explosion"` is still one name — prefer
   `"myevents/explosion"` style or unique long filenames like the `sfx`
   pack does). `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
3. **Wrong name format in `play_sound`.** No `sounds/` root, no extension,
   no `_N` suffix, no pack prefix — any of those present means silence,
   not an error. `[VERIFIED]`
4. **Variant numbering gaps.** `name_1.ogg` + `name_3.ogg` without
   `name_2.ogg` loads only `name_1.ogg` and stops at the gap — silently.
   DO number variants densely from 0 or 1. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
5. **Stereo positional sound.** Stereo files ignore world position. A
   positional effect must be mono; test from a distance. `[DOC]`
6. **`master` as a channel.** `audio.play_sound_2d("click", 1.0, 1.0,
   "master")` plays nothing. Channels are `ui`/`regular`/`ambient`/`music`
   only. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
7. **24-bit WAV.** OpenAL path supports 8/16-bit WAV only; a 24-bit file
   fails to load (breaking pack load if preloaded). DO convert to 16-bit
   WAV or OGG. `[DOC]`
8. **Restarting a stream while it plays.** One stream file = one speaker;
   call `audio.stop(old_id)` before playing the same file again, or keep
   ONE long-lived looping speaker and control it via volume.
   `[DOC]`
9. **Missing preloaded file breaks pack load.** `"could not to find sound"`
   is a hard failure at load time. Keep preload entries and files in sync.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
10. **Ambience on the wrong channel.** Loops started on the default
    `regular` channel pause with the game; background weather/music belongs
    on `ambient`/`music`. `[DOC]`
11. **Starting ambience in `on_world_open`.** The `regular` and `ambient`
    channels are reset when the level screen opens — moments after
    `on_world_open` fires (the gap is the initial chunk loading, ~0.5 s
    observed). Any loop started there is silently destroyed. DO start
    ambience in `on_hud_open` (hud.lua). `[VERIFIED: engine source,
    Engine::setScreen]`
12. **Typos in material sound names degrade silently.** A material's
    `steps-sound` that matches no file does not break pack load (unlike
    preload entries) — the step sound is simply missing in game. DO copy
    names from your `preload.json`/file tree, not from memory.
    `[VERIFIED: material sounds are engine-requested assets]`

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO use preloaded Sounds for short effects and Streams for long audio.
- DO name preloaded sounds exactly `name` / `subfolder/name` — no pack
  prefix, no `sounds/` root, no extension, no `_N`.
- DO namespace sound and stream names across packs (subfolder or unique
  long filenames); the namespace is flat and collision-prone.
- DO ship positional effects in MONO and test them from a distance.
- DO keep variant numbering dense (`name.ogg` or `name_0.ogg`, then
  `name_1..N` without gaps).
- DO start long loops muted and ramp volume from a tick handler.
- DO start ambient/music world loops from `on_hud_open` (hud.lua), never
  from `on_world_open` — the level-screen reset wipes `regular` and
  `ambient` moments after the world opens.
- AVOID `preload.json` entries for block-material sounds — the engine
  requests them automatically.
- AVOID passing `master` (or an invented channel) to any play call.
- AVOID preloading minutes-long audio as Sounds (RAM) — stream it.
- AVOID re-playing a stream file while its previous speaker is alive.
- AVOID trusting that a play call succeeded — check the speaker id while
  debugging, the API never raises on failure.

## Upstream pointers (read before writing real audio code)

All paths are files in the VoxelCore engine repository
(github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore), NOT in this guide. The Russian docs are
usually richer and fresher — prefer `doc/ru/` when they disagree.

| Topic | EN | RU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio system, channels, speaker semantics, full `audio.*` API | `doc/en/audio.md` | `doc/ru/audio.md` |
| Preload entries, `keep-pcm`, sound variants note | `doc/en/assets-preload.md` | `doc/ru/assets-preload.md` |
| Block material fields (`steps-sound`, ...) | `doc/en/block-properties.md` | `doc/ru/block-properties.md` |
| Backend/engine config (`[audio] enabled=false`) | `doc/en/console.md` | `doc/ru/console.md` |

Where this guide goes beyond the upstream text (the three stream address
forms, the silent `0`-return contract, the flat namespace and overwrite
behavior, the variant-gap rule, the automatic loading of material sounds,
the `hit-sound` fallback, the screen-switch channel reset and the
world-open event order), the claims were verified against the engine
source at the time of writing — re-verify against your engine version if
behavior seems to differ.

Real usage to learn from: `wooden_meat_game` — `content/my_pack/`
(`preload.json` `"sounds": ["shotgun"]`, `scripts/shotgun.lua`,
`scripts/components/turret_targeting.lua`) for preloaded sounds, and
`content/sfx/` (`modules/ambient.lua` started from `scripts/hud.lua`, no
preload at all) for streams, volume automation and the `on_hud_open`
ambience pattern.


<!-- ===== docs/13-sound-creation.md ===== -->

# 13. Creating Audio at Runtime (PCMStream, Mic Input)

> **MANDATORY PREREQUISITES — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md),
> [08-pitfalls.md](08-pitfalls.md) AND
> [12-sounds.md](12-sounds.md). 01 defines the ID rules and trust labels
> this guide relies on; 08 lists the real failure modes behind every
> DO/AVOID note; 12 defines the Sound vs Stream mental model, channels,
> speaker semantics and the stream address resolution rules this file
> builds on. If you received only this file, fetch and read all three
> before writing any code.

This document covers GENERATING audio inside the engine instead of shipping
recorded files: building an `audio.PCMStream` in Lua, feeding raw PCM
samples into it, publishing it as a playable stream alias or materializing
it as a Sound, plus microphone input. Use it when the audio does not exist
as a file: synthesized tones and noise, DSP-processed signals, audio
received from the network or the microphone, anything computed at runtime.
If the audio already exists as an OGG/WAV file, ship the file and use
`preload.json` / `play_stream` (12-sounds.md) — that path is simpler,
cheaper and covers the overwhelming majority of packs.

## When to generate audio instead of shipping files

`[DOC]` Generate at runtime only when one of these holds:

- the audio is computed (sirens, tones, noise beds, procedural effects);
- the audio arrives from outside the pack (network stream, microphone);
- you must process an existing sound in ways files cannot express.

Everything else is a file + `preload.json` problem. Runtime generation
costs CPU, RAM and code, and its failure modes are silent like all audio
failures (12-sounds.md Pitfalls #1).

## `audio.PCMStream`: the object

| Member | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `audio.PCMStream(sample_rate, channels, bits)` | Constructor: sample rate in Hz; `channels`: 1 = mono, 2 = stereo; `bits`: 8 or 16 |
| `stream:feed(data)` | Append PCM bytes (a `Bytearray`) to the stream buffer |
| `stream:share(alias)` | Publish the stream under an alias address for `audio.play_stream` |
| `stream:create_sound(name)` | Materialize the PCM fed SO FAR into a Sound registered under `name` |

`[DOC: audio.md]` Verified semantics the upstream doc does not spell out:

1. `share(alias)` stores the stream in the asset registry that
   `audio.play_stream` consults FIRST, before pack paths — the shared-alias
   row of the stream address table in 12-sounds.md.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source, libaudio.cpp]`
2. On the headless backend `share()` is a silent no-op: the alias is NOT
   registered and playback would return `0` anyway. Do not expect
   generated audio to work in headless test runs.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source, lua_type_pcmstream.cpp]`
3. `create_sound(name)` registers a normal multi-speaker Sound under `name`
   in the SAME flat global namespace as preloaded sounds — playable with
   `audio.play_sound(name)` with NO `preload.json` entry, and subject to
   the same overwrite-on-collision rule (12-sounds.md Pitfalls #2).
   `[VERIFIED: engine source, lua_type_pcmstream.cpp]`
4. `create_sound(name)` captures only the samples fed BEFORE the call;
   feeding afterwards does not change the created Sound.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
5. A second `share()` or `create_sound()` with the same string silently
   replaces the earlier registration — there is no error and no merge.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

## Sample format rules

| Parameter | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `sample_rate` | integer Hz (e.g. 44100); must match your sample-count math |
| `channels` | 1 = mono, 2 = stereo — positional playback REQUIRES mono (12-sounds.md) |
| `bits` | 8 or 16 only |
| 16-bit samples | write through `I16view` (or `U16view`) over the `Bytearray`, never as raw bytes |
| Buffer size | `bits / 8` bytes per sample per channel (`2` for 16-bit mono) |

`[DOC]` 24-bit (or wider) PCM has no place anywhere in the audio system:
24-bit WAV is unsupported by OpenAL (12-sounds.md), and `PCMStream` accepts
8/16 bits only.

## Worked example: a generated tone

`[DOC: audio.md]` Minimal working example from the upstream doc (formatting
normalized):

```lua
local max_amplitude = 32767
local sample_rate = 44100
local total_samples = sample_rate * 5
local bytes = Bytearray(total_samples * 2)
local samples = I16view(bytes)

for i = 1, total_samples do
    samples[i] = math.sin(i * math.pi * 2 / sample_rate * 400) * max_amplitude
end

local stream = audio.PCMStream(sample_rate, 1, 16)
stream:feed(bytes)
stream:share("test-stream")

audio.play_stream_2d("test-stream", 1.0, 1.0, "ui")
```

What it does, step by step:

- allocates a `Bytearray` of `total_samples * 2` bytes — 5 s of 16-bit mono;
- writes a 400 Hz sine through `I16view` (never raw bytes for 16-bit);
- feeds the buffer into a `PCMStream(44100, 1, 16)` and publishes it as the
  alias `"test-stream"`;
- plays it as a non-positional stream on the `ui` channel.

To materialize the same buffer as a Sound instead (multi-speaker, played by
name): `[OBSERVED: API shape per engine source]`

```lua
stream:create_sound("my_pack:tone")
audio.play_sound_2d("my_pack:tone", 1.0, 1.0)
```

## `share()` vs `create_sound()`

| | `share(alias)` | `create_sound(name)` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Played via | `audio.play_stream` (alias resolved first) | `audio.play_sound` |
| Speaker model | ONE speaker per stream at a time | Many speakers at once |
| RAM | backend reads the buffer as it plays | fully buffered as a Sound |
| Live updates | you can keep `feed()`ing while it plays | frozen at call time |

`[VERIFIED: engine source]` Decision rule follows the 12-sounds.md mental
model: repeated one-shots → `create_sound`; long, generated or
still-growing audio → `share`. The upstream doc explicitly names network
audio streaming as the intended use of the PCMStream interface — feeding
while playing (radio-style) is the designed pattern, not a hack. `[DOC:
audio.md]`

## Naming: the namespaces you are writing into

- Shared aliases and created-sound names are runtime REGISTRY keys, not
  files; they never appear in `preload.json`.
- DO prefix BOTH with your pack id (`"my_pack:tone"`): aliases resolve
  before file paths and created sounds share the flat preload namespace —
  an unprefixed name can collide with another pack's file or sound and be
  silently overwritten (12-sounds.md Pitfalls #2). `[VERIFIED: engine
  source]`
- An alias shadows a bare file path with the same string at resolution
  time; resolution order is fixed (12-sounds.md Streams table).

## Microphone input (pointer only)

`audio.input.request_open(callback)` asks the user for recording permission
and passes an access token to the callback; `audio.input.fetch(token,
max_read_size)` then returns new PCM chunks you can `feed()` into a
PCMStream. This is niche for content packs and gated by user consent — read
`doc/ru/audio.md` ("Запись звука") before using. `[DOC]`

## Pitfalls (creation-specific)

1. **Unprefixed alias or sound name.** Both registries are flat global
   namespaces with silent overwrite on collision — DO prefix with the pack
   id. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
2. **Headless `share()` no-op.** Generated aliases do not register on the
   headless backend; automated test runs will silently have no generated
   audio. `[VERIFIED: engine source, lua_type_pcmstream.cpp]`
3. **Feeding after `create_sound`.** The Sound is a snapshot of the buffer
   at call time; late feeds change nothing. Keep feeding only streams you
   published with `share()`. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
4. **Raw byte writes to 16-bit samples.** Use `I16view`/`U16view` over the
   `Bytearray`; byte-wise writes produce garbage. `[DOC]`
5. **Stereo PCM for positional playback.** Stereo ignores source position
   (12-sounds.md) — generated positional audio must be built with
   `channels = 1`. `[DOC]`
6. **`get_duration` returns `0` for shared streams.** The length of
   generated audio is legitimately unknown to the engine; not an error.
   `[DOC]`

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO ship OGG/WAV files whenever the audio exists as a file; generate only
  what cannot be shipped.
- DO prefix shared aliases and created-sound names with the pack id.
- DO write 16-bit samples via `I16view`/`U16view` over the `Bytearray`.
- DO keep one long-lived PCMStream and keep feeding it for radio-style
  audio — that is the intended pattern, not a hack.
- AVOID `share()`ing and expecting it to work in headless test runs.
- AVOID feeding after `create_sound()` and expecting the Sound to change.
- AVOID unprefixed names (flat namespaces, silent overwrites).
- AVOID stereo PCM for positional playback.

## Upstream pointers (read before writing real audio code)

All paths are files in the VoxelCore engine repository
(github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore), NOT in this guide. The Russian docs are
usually richer and fresher — prefer `doc/ru/` when they disagree.

| Topic | EN | RU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audio.PCMStream`, mic input, generation example | `doc/en/audio.md` | `doc/ru/audio.md` |

Where this guide goes beyond the upstream text (the registry semantics of
`share`/`create_sound`, the headless `share()` no-op, the snapshot-at-call
rule, the overwrite-on-collision behavior), the claims were verified
against the engine source (`lua_type_pcmstream.cpp`, `libaudio.cpp`,
`Assets.hpp`) at the time of writing — re-verify against your engine
version if behavior seems to differ.


<!-- ===== docs/14-models.md ===== -->

# 14. Models (VCM, OBJ, Custom Block and Item Models)

> **MANDATORY PREREQUISITES — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md) AND
> [08-pitfalls.md](08-pitfalls.md). 01 defines the ID rules, reserved names
> and trust labels this file relies on; 08 lists the real failure modes
> behind every DO/AVOID note. For the block `texture-faces` order read
> [03-blocks.md](03-blocks.md); for entity/skeleton usage read
> [10-entities.md](10-entities.md). If you received only this file, fetch
> and read the prerequisites before writing any code.

This document covers 3D models shipped by a content pack: the `models/`
folder, the VCM text format, OBJ usage, custom block models, item models
and VCM-embedded skeletons. Models are what make a block look non-cubic,
an item appear in the player's hand, and an entity take shape.

## Where model files live and how names resolve

| Fact | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Folder | `models/` in the pack folder — engine constant `MODELS_FOLDER` `[VERIFIED: engine source]` |
| Asset name | the file stem: `models/box.vcm` → model `"box"` |
| Extension order | `.vec3` → `.obj` → `.xml` → `.vcm` — first EXISTING file wins `[VERIFIED: engine source, assetload::model]` |
| Missing file | hard failure `could not to find model "<name>"` — breaks pack/world load `[VERIFIED: engine source]` |
| Bare-name resolution | `paths.find()` across ALL packs by content-source priority — flat, collision-prone namespace, same idea as sounds |

Rules:

1. `.vec3` and `.xml` are legacy engine formats. DO NOT create them in
   packs; ship VCM or OBJ only. `[DOC]`
2. Model names containing `:` are NEVER auto-loaded for blocks, items or
   entities — the loader skips them (they exist for engine-internal
   assets). A pack CANNOT write `other_pack:model` into `model-name` and
   expect it to load. `[VERIFIED: engine source, AssetsLoader::addDefaults]`
3. Consequence of rule 2: model names are bare and global. Two packs
   shipping `models/box.vcm` means the higher-priority pack's file wins
   for BOTH, silently. DO make model names unique — subfolder-style names
   work: `"turret/base"` loads `models/turret/base.vcm`.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
4. `preload.json` has a `"models"` key for EXPLICIT preloading:
   `"models": ["name", {"name": "name", "squash": true}]`. Only needed
   for multi-part (boned) VCMs you want usable as ONE model — see VCM
   bones. Models referenced by blocks/items/skeletons load automatically.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

## Who triggers loading (auto-requests)

| Referenced by | Auto-load rule |
| --- | --- |
| Block variant `"model": "custom"` + `"model-name"` | requested when the name has no `:` |
| Item `"model-name"` | requested when the name has no `:` |
| Entity `"skeleton-name"` | requested as a MODEL (expected: VCM with bones) when the name has no `:` |
| `skeletons/*.json` bone `"model"` fields | model per bone, name stripped of the `.<bone>` suffix |
| `preload.json` `"models"` | loaded explicitly at startup |

`[VERIFIED: engine source, AssetsLoader::addDefaults + assetload::skeleton]`

## Block custom models

Block JSON (full block reference in 03-blocks.md):

```json
{
    "model": "custom",
    "model-name": "destroyer_belt"
}
```

`model-name` is read ONLY when `"model"` is `"custom"` — on any other model
type it is ignored. `[VERIFIED: user first-hand]`

| `model` value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| none | invisible block |
| block | default cube (default) |
| xsprite | X-shape (grass) |
| aabb | box shaped as the block hitbox |
| custom | custom model via `model-name` |

`[VERIFIED: engine source, Block.hpp]` A typo in the `model` value is logged
(`unknown model: <value>`) and the block silently becomes `none` —
invisible, NO load error. `[VERIFIED: engine source, BlockLoader]`

The `"model-primitives"` JSON property still works but is officially
deprecated in favor of VCM — DO NOT use it in new packs.
`[DOC: block-models.md WARNING]`

### Textures inside models

| Texture string | Resolved as |
| --- | --- |
| `$0` .. `$5` | the BLOCK's own texture-faces, SAME order as the texture-faces JSON |
| `blocks:<name>` | texture from the blocks atlas (UVs remapped into the atlas region) |
| bare name (`models/box`) | standalone texture auto-loaded from `textures/<name>` of the packs |

`[VERIFIED: engine source, ModelsGenerator + ContentGfxCache +
request_textures]` `$N` binding is a BLOCK-model mechanism — in item or
skeleton models a `$N` mesh texture is never bound (see Item models).

Verified details:

- Box sides default to `$0`..`$5`; tri/rect default to `$0`.
- `$N` with N outside 0..5 stays unbound — silently no texture.
- A bare texture name without `textures/<name>.png` is logged at load and
  the mesh stays untextured — NOT a hard failure.
  `[VERIFIED: engine source, assetload::texture]`

Scale: one block = 1.0 unit; a block custom model should fit the
1×1×1 cube (the example `box.vcm` spans 0..1). Coordinates are NOT
normalized. `[OBSERVED: stock and example packs]`

## VCM format

A text format describing a model from primitives; replaces the deprecated
`model-primitives`. Syntax: `@primitive attr (v1,v2,...) attr2 "string" {
nested... }` — think XML without a single root; multiple root elements are
allowed. `[DOC: vcm.md]`

> By default texture coordinates derive from primitive sizes. Above 1.0
> the result is UNDEFINED and may change between engine versions — use
> `region` or `region-scale`. `[DOC: vcm.md NOTE]`

### `box`

```vcm
@box from (0, 0, 0) to (1, 1, 1) texture "entities/nepis" {
    @part tags (north) texture "entities/nepis_face"
}
```
(from `wooden_meat_game`, `models/nepis.vcm` — an entity texture example)

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| from / to | opposite corners of the box |
| origin | rotation pivot; default: box center |
| rotate | degrees per axis `(45,0,0)` or quaternion `(x,y,z,w)` |
| texture | texture for ALL sides; default: `$0`..`$5` per side |
| shading | `shading off` disables shading |
| delete | remove sides by name: top, bottom, east, west, north, south |

`@part` (nested in `box`) overrides per-side properties:

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| tags | sides to affect: top, bottom, east, west, north, south |
| texture | side texture; default: `$<side index>` |
| region / region-scale | UV region inside the chosen texture |

Side indices match the texture-faces order `[VERIFIED: engine source,
vcm.cpp side_indices]`:

| Index | Side | Face |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | west | −X |
| 1 | east | +X |
| 2 | bottom | −Y |
| 3 | top | +Y |
| 4 | north | −Z |
| 5 | south | +Z |

### `rect` (parallelogram)

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| from | start point |
| right / up | X and Y vectors — also define width/height |
| texture / region / region-scale | as above; default `$0` |
| shading / flip / normal / cull-face | `flip v` mirrors the UV region vertically |

### `tri` (triangle)

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| a / b / c | corner points, e.g. `a (0,0,0)` |
| uv | six numbers, 2 per point: `uv (0,0, 1,0, 1,1)` |
| texture / region / region-scale | as above; default `$0` |
| shading / normal / cull-face | as above |

Tri UVs do NOT depend on shape or size (unlike rect/box). `[DOC]`

Shared primitive properties `[DOC: vcm.md]`:

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `shading off` | disable shading on the primitive |
| `normal (x,y,z)` | override the normal vector |
| `cull-face front` / `cull-face off` | which side is culled; `off` = two-sided |

## VCM bones (a skeleton inside the model)

`@bone` wraps primitives and other bones `[DOC: vcm.md]`:

- WITH `name` → enters the model's skeleton (rigging-compatible).
- WITHOUT a name → "dissolved": its transforms apply to children, nothing
  enters the skeleton.
- A `root` bone is created automatically for the whole model.
- Bone properties: `move`, `scale` (applied BEFORE move), `rotate`.

Verified consequences `[VERIFIED: engine source, load_vcm_model]`:

1. A VCM with named bones (more than one part, not squashed) stores its
   parts as `<model>.<bone>` assets plus a skeleton under the bare model
   name — and NO single model under the bare name. DO NOT reference such
   a model from a block or item: the model will not be found. Use it as
   an entity skeleton (10-entities.md) instead.
2. `"squash": true` in `preload.json` merges the VCM back into ONE model
   under the bare name — usable as a block/item model, no skeleton.
3. Unnamed bones keep the model single-part — safe for blocks/items.

## OBJ

Verified against the engine's parser, the supported subset is: `v`, `vn`,
`vt`, `f` and `usemtl`. `[VERIFIED: engine source, obj.cpp]`

- `usemtl <name>` — the name IS the texture reference (same three forms:
  `$N` / `blocks:name` / bare name). MTL FILES ARE NOT PARSED — `mtllib`
  lines are ignored and no `.mtl` file is needed. Real example:
  `my_pack/models/shotgun.obj` (a Blender 4.0.2 export) references
  `shotgun.mtl` that is not even shipped; its `usemtl Material` resolves
  to `textures/Material.png`, which is shipped. `[OBSERVED]`
- A bare texture name with no `textures/<name>.png` logs an error at load
  and the mesh stays untextured (not a hard failure).
  `[VERIFIED: engine source, assetload::texture]`
- Models are used at their authored scale; block custom models should fit
  the 1×1×1 cube. `[OBSERVED]`

## Item models

`model-name` on an item (04-items.md) selects the 3D model shown in the
player's hand: the engine's own `hud.lua` renders `item.model_name(id)` on
the hand bone. `[VERIFIED: engine source + res/scripts/hud.lua]`

| Case | Model used |
| --- | --- |
| No `model-name` | a GENERATED model stored as `<packid>:<item>.model`: block-icon items reuse the block's model (scaled to 0.2); sprite-icon items get a flat quad textured with the icon |
| `"model-name": "shotgun"` | `models/shotgun.*` of the packs, auto-loaded (no `:` in the name) |

`[VERIFIED: engine source, ModelsGenerator + ItemDef]` The generated
default name contains `:`, so it is never file-loaded — it exists only as
the generated asset. `[VERIFIED]`

Real example (`wooden_meat_game`, `content/my_pack/items/shotgun.json`):
`[OBSERVED]`

```json
{
    "icon-type": "sprite",
    "icon": "items:shotgun",
    "stack-size": 1,
    "model-name": "shotgun"
}
```

## Models and entities

- ALL files in a pack's `skeletons/` folder are auto-loaded as skeletons
  named `<packid>:<file stem>` — no preload entry needed.
  `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
- Entity `skeleton-name` defaults to the entity's own id — so entity
  `my_pack:turret` automatically picks up the skeleton `my_pack:turret`
  from `skeletons/turret.json`. That name coincidence is how the example
  pack wires its turret and nepis models without any explicit field.
  `[VERIFIED: engine source, Entities.cpp]`
- `skeleton-name` may also point at a bare VCM name — the engine then
  expects a VCM WITH bones and requests it as a model.
  `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
- A missing skeleton: WARNING if the name equals the entity id, hard
  ERROR otherwise. `[VERIFIED: engine source, Entities.cpp]`
- Skeleton bones reference models by name (stripped of the `.<bone>`
  suffix) and those models auto-load — `skeletons/turret.json` pulls
  `models/turret.vcm` and `models/shotgun.obj`. `[VERIFIED: engine source,
  assetload::skeleton]`

Stock example: `res/content/base/entities/falling_block.json` uses
`"skeleton-name": "base:block"`. `[OBSERVED]` Bone ANIMATION is covered in
11-animation.md; the skeleton JSON format in 10-entities.md and
`doc/ru/rigging.md`.

## Pitfalls (models-specific)

1. **Missing model file breaks world load.** `could not to find model`
   is a hard failure for any auto-requested or preloaded model. Keep
   references and files in sync. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
2. **Flat global namespace with no pack prefix.** Bare model names resolve
   across packs by priority; a colliding name silently shadows another
   pack's model — and you CANNOT fix it with `pack:name` (auto-load skips
   `:` names). DO use unique names or subfolders.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
3. **`model-name` on a non-custom block.** Read only when
   `"model": "custom"`; otherwise ignored. `[VERIFIED: user first-hand]`
4. **Typo in the `model` value.** Logged as `unknown model` and the block
   becomes `none` — invisible, no load error. Copy values from this table,
   not from memory. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
5. **Named-bone VCM as a block/item model.** Such a file stores parts as
   `<model>.<bone>` and NO model under the bare name — the block/item
   model is missing. DO use `"squash": true` or keep bones unnamed.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
6. **`$N` outside 0..5 or outside block models.** Silently unbound — no
   texture, no error. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
7. **Expecting MTL materials.** The OBJ parser never reads `.mtl`;
   `usemtl` names are texture asset names. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
8. **VCM UVs beyond 1.0.** Undefined per upstream; use `region` /
   `region-scale`. `[DOC]`
9. **Missing model textures fail silently.** Logged at load, mesh stays
   untextured. Check the log when a model renders untextured.
   `[VERIFIED: engine source]`
10. **Legacy extensions.** `.vec3`/`.xml` win over `.vcm` in the extension
    order — an old file with the same stem silently overrides your VCM.
    DO NOT ship them in packs. `[VERIFIED: engine source]`

## DO / AVOID summary

- DO ship `.vcm` (or `.obj`) under `models/` with unique names (subfolders
  count as part of the name).
- DO use `$0`..`$5` in block custom models to reuse the block's
  texture-faces; `blocks:name` for atlas textures; bare names only with a
  matching file under `textures/`.
- DO keep block/item models single-part; use named bones only for entity
  skeletons.
- DO export OBJ without expecting `.mtl` to be read; name `usemtl` after
  your texture.
- AVOID `model-primitives` in new packs (deprecated by VCM).
- AVOID `:` inside your own model names (auto-load skips them).
- AVOID default UVs beyond 1.0 — use `region` / `region-scale`.
- AVOID shipping `.vec3`/`.xml` models in packs.

## Upstream pointers (read before writing real models)

All paths are files in the VoxelCore engine repository
(github.com/MihailRis/voxelcore), NOT in this guide. The Russian docs are
usually richer and fresher — prefer `doc/ru/` when they disagree.

| Topic | EN | RU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VCM format, primitives, bones | `doc/en/vcm.md` | `doc/ru/vcm.md` |
| Deprecated `model-primitives` | `doc/en/block-models.md` | `doc/ru/block-models.md` |
| Skeleton/rigging format | `doc/en/rigging.md` | `doc/ru/rigging.md` |
| Entity `skeleton-name` | `doc/en/entity-properties.md` | `doc/ru/entity-properties.md` |

Where this guide goes beyond the upstream text (extension order, auto-load
rules, the flat namespace and the `:` skip, texture binding `$N` /
`blocks:` / bare name, the single-part storage rule, MTL behavior, item
model generation), the claims were verified against the engine source
(`AssetsLoader`, `assetload_funcs`, `vcm.cpp`, `obj.cpp`, `ModelsGenerator`,
`ContentGfxCache`, `Entities`) at the time of writing — re-verify against
your engine version if behavior seems to differ.

Real usage to learn from: `wooden_meat_game` — `content/my_pack/models/`
(`box.vcm`, `nepis.vcm`, `turret.vcm`, `shotgun.obj`), `skeletons/`
(`turret.json`, `nepis.json`), `items/shotgun.json`, `textures/`
(`Material.png`, `models/`, `items/`); engine stock `res/models/`
(`block.vec3`, `drop-item.vec3`, `human.vcm`) and
`res/content/base/entities/falling_block.json` (`skeleton-name`).


<!-- ===== docs/08-pitfalls.md ===== -->

# 08. Pitfalls and Pre-flight Checklist

> **MANDATORY PAIR — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md) (ID rules, reserved names,
> trust labels). Every other document in this guide also assumes you have
> read THIS file. If you received only this file, fetch and read 01 before
> writing any code.

Every entry below is a real failure mode — either documented upstream, thrown
by the engine, or observed in real packs. Treat each AVOID as a hard rule.

## Fatal mistakes

1. **Editing `content.json`.** It is auto-generated and used to convert world
   saves. Manual edits corrupt worlds irreversibly (upstream warning).
   AVOID creating, editing, or deleting it in source repos.
2. **Missing `package.json`.** A folder without it is not a pack — the scanner
   skips it. DO always start from the manifest.
3. **Invalid pack ID.** Outside `a-z0-9_`, starting with a digit, or shorter
   than 2 / longer than 24 chars breaks registration. Reserved IDs (`res`,
   `user`, `world`, `project`, `config`, `core`) are unavailable. `[VERIFIED]`
4. **`texture-faces` with fewer than 6 entries.** The engine throws
   "texture-faces requires 6 elements" and the pack fails to load.
   `[OBSERVED: engine source]`
5. **Using `texture` and `texture-faces` together.** Documented as incompatible;
   pick one. `[DOC]`
6. **Paths or extensions in texture names.** `"texture": "blocks/dirt.png"` is
   wrong. The value is a NAME resolved inside an atlas: `"dirt"` or
   `"blocks:dirt"` depending on context. `[VERIFIED]`
7. **Using `base:*` properties without depending on `base`.** `base:durability`
   and `base:loot` are registered by the `base` pack; without
   `"dependencies": ["base"]` they are not guaranteed to exist. `[VERIFIED]`
8. **Loot referencing a block instead of its item.** `base:loot[].item` needs an
   ITEM id; a block's item is `<pack>:<block>.item`. `[VERIFIED]`

## Likely-wrong assumptions (seen in practice)

9. **Assuming folder name = pack ID.** The engine keys packs by the `"id"` in
   `package.json`; the folder name is free-form and has NO meaning to the
   engine. In real packs the folder name almost always DIFFERS from the ID
   (e.g. folder `kompot_0f9103ff-1.2.2` ships `"id": "kompot"`), and exact
   matches are rare. NEVER infer a pack's ID from its folder name — read the
   manifest. `[OBSERVED]`
10. **Assuming `icon.png` must be 128x128.** It is a recommendation; 64x64 and
    210x208 exist in working packs. Keep it square. `[OBSERVED]`
11. **Assuming texture sizes are enforced.** Stock uses 16x16; other sizes are
    uncharted. DO stay 16x16 for blocks/items.
12. **Assuming `version` matters for pack resolution.** When two sources carry
    the same pack ID, priority decides; version is ignored. `[DOC]`
13. **Assuming a pack needs content.** A folder containing ONLY `package.json`
    is a complete, valid, loadable pack — nothing else is required. Blocks,
    items, textures, config and code are all optional extras (Kompot ships no
    blocks/items; confirmed first-hand). `[VERIFIED]`
14. **Inventing dependency version operators.** Only `@>=x.y` and `*` are
    documented. AVOID `<`, `<=`, `=`, ranges. `[DOC]`
15. **Capitalizing captions yourself.** Docs recommend lowercase captions; the
    engine upper-cases for display. Localization keys must match the lowercase
    caption string. `[DOC]`
16. **Preloading auto-loaded assets.** Block/item atlas textures are picked up
    automatically; preloading them is noise (upstream warns to keep preload
    minimal). `[DOC]`
17. **Putting `pack_id:` into `<image src>` or `menu.page`.** These do NOT use
    the pack namespace: `src` without a colon is a global texture name; `src`
    with a colon is `atlas_name:tile_name`; `menu.page` takes a bare page name
    scanned across all packs. Pack-qualified ids belong only to layout ids
    (`hud.show_overlay("pack:layout")`) and document paths
    (`gui.load_document`). See 09-hud-and-ui.md. `[VERIFIED]`
18. **Spelling the animation folder or preload key `animations`.** The engine
    constant is `animation` (singular): pack folder `animation/`, `preload.json`
    key `"animation"`. An upstream quirk you must reproduce. `[VERIFIED]`
    The full animation reference is 11-animation.md.

## JSON hygiene

- AVOID trailing commas and comments — block/item files are strict JSON.
- DO keep UTF-8 (localization values are non-ASCII routinely).
- DO keep one definition per file; the file name is the content name.

## Pre-flight checklist (run before delivering a pack)

Manifest:
- [ ] `package.json` exists, parses, has `id`/`title`/`version`.
- [ ] `id` passes rules and is not reserved. Folder name is free-form — it
      does NOT need to equal `id`.
- [ ] `dependencies` lists every pack whose `pack:` references you use.

Content:
- [ ] Every `blocks/*.json` and `items/*.json` uses only properties documented
      in 03/04 (or upstream docs) — nothing invented.
- [ ] `texture-faces` arrays have exactly 6 entries in west/east/bottom/top/
      north/south order.
- [ ] No `texture` + `texture-faces` in the same block.
- [ ] Every texture/icon name resolves to a real PNG in `textures/blocks/` or
      `textures/items/`.
- [ ] `base:*` properties used only with `base` dependency; loot items use
      `.item` suffix where needed.

Assets & config:
- [ ] `icon.png` present at pack root (square).
- [ ] `preload.json` (if present) contains only genuinely needed entries.
- [ ] `texts/*.txt` keys match captions exactly (lowercase, spaces not
      underscores).
- [ ] No `content.json` committed from your side.

UI (09):
- [ ] Layout XMLs sit at `layouts/*.xml` (flat folder); menu pages at
      `layouts/pages/`.
- [ ] No pack id in `menu.page` names or in `<image src>` values.
- [ ] Animation folder/key spelled `animation` (singular), if used.

Runtime:
- [ ] Pack loads without errors in the engine log/console.
- [ ] Blocks appear in the content/inventory screen and place correctly.
- [ ] Loot drops, lights emit, plants sit on ground — as designed.

## Debugging hints

- Load errors are printed by the engine with the failing pack and file name
  (e.g. unknown model, JSON parse errors, missing textures render as
  `notfound`). Read the console output first. `[OBSERVED]`
- A pack that loads but shows missing textures/`notfound` icons indicates a
  name/folder mismatch (03/05 rules), not a manifest problem.
- The in-game console and engine logging are documented in the engine repo
  (`doc/ru/console.md`, mirrored as `doc/en/console.md`) — out of scope here.


<!-- ===== docs/06-walkthrough.md ===== -->

# 06. Walkthrough: Build a Complete Minimal Pack

> **MANDATORY PREREQUISITES — DO NOT SKIP.** This file assumes you have read
> [01-engine-overview.md](01-engine-overview.md) AND
> [08-pitfalls.md](08-pitfalls.md). 01 defines the ID rules, reserved names
> and trust labels this file relies on; 08 lists the real failure modes
> behind every DO/AVOID note. Skipping either is the most common reason
> models generate broken packs from this guide. If you received only this
> file, fetch and read both before writing any code.

Goal: a working pack `my_first_pack` that adds:
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_ore` — a stone-like ore cube,
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_lamp` — a glowing cube,
- block `my_first_pack:ruby_flower` — a decorative plant,
- item `my_first_pack:ruby` — a plain sprite item,
- a pack icon.

No Lua, no models, no sounds — pure declarative content. Every file below is
complete and final; assemble them in order and the pack works.

## Step 0 — Choose the location

DO develop in the user content folder so any world can use the pack:

```text
$HOME/.voxeng/content/my_first_pack/
```

(Linux path; `user:content` source, priority above `res:content` — see
02-pack-structure.md.) The folder name is free-form — it does NOT need to
match the pack ID (real packs rarely match). This walkthrough uses the ID as
the folder name purely for tidiness.

## Step 1 — package.json (pack becomes loadable)

File: `my_first_pack/package.json`

```json
{
    "id": "my_first_pack",
    "title": "My First Pack",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "creator": "Your Name",
    "description": "Ruby ore, lamp, flower and a ruby item",
    "dependencies": ["base"]
}
```

`dependencies: ["base"]` is REQUIRED here because the blocks below use
`base:durability` and `base:loot` (properties registered by `base`).

STOP and verify: the pack must already appear in the engine's content menu with
no other files at all.

## Step 2 — Textures

Create two folders and four PNG files, 16x16, RGBA:

```text
textures/blocks/ruby_ore.png
textures/blocks/ruby_lamp.png
textures/blocks/ruby_flower.png
textures/items/ruby.png
```
